.claude/CLAUDE.md:145: trailing whitespace.
+
.claude/CLAUDE.md:146: trailing whitespace.
+An operator (or AI helper) can read/write **arbitrary** Modbus registers on a running daemon
.claude/CLAUDE.md:147: trailing whitespace.
+without editing config, via an MQTT5 request/response exchange. Design reference:
.claude/CLAUDE.md:148: trailing whitespace.
+`.claude/plans/quiet-churning-snail.md`.
.claude/CLAUDE.md:149: trailing whitespace.
+
.claude/CLAUDE.md:150: trailing whitespace.

.claude/CLAUDE.md:151: trailing whitespace.
+  (`RpcMode` in `config.hpp`). `disabled` (default) → the connection stays MQTT **3.1.1**, no RPC
.claude/CLAUDE.md:152: trailing whitespace.

.claude/CLAUDE.md:153: trailing whitespace.

.claude/CLAUDE.md:154: trailing whitespace.

.claude/CLAUDE.md:155: trailing whitespace.
+  subscribers downstream are unaffected (the broker strips v5-only properties for them).
.claude/CLAUDE.md:156: trailing whitespace.

.claude/CLAUDE.md:157: trailing whitespace.

.claude/CLAUDE.md:158: trailing whitespace.

.claude/CLAUDE.md:159: trailing whitespace.

.claude/CLAUDE.md:160: trailing whitespace.

.claude/CLAUDE.md:161: trailing whitespace.

.claude/CLAUDE.md:162: trailing whitespace.

.claude/CLAUDE.md:163: trailing whitespace.

.claude/CLAUDE.md:164: trailing whitespace.

.claude/CLAUDE.md:167: trailing whitespace.

.claude/CLAUDE.md:168: trailing whitespace.

+### Test timing & synchronization
.claude/CLAUDE.md:284: trailing whitespace.
+
.claude/CLAUDE.md:285: trailing whitespace.
+Time-dependent tests are **not** written with raw sleeps and fixed durations — everything goes
.claude/CLAUDE.md:286: trailing whitespace.
+through the `timing` helper (`unittests/timing.{hpp,cpp}`) and condition-variable wait helpers, so
.claude/CLAUDE.md:287: trailing whitespace.
+the suite runs correctly whether the machine is fast or a slow ARM CI box.
.claude/CLAUDE.md:288: trailing whitespace.
+
.claude/CLAUDE.md:289: trailing whitespace.
+The governing rule is that **raising `MQM_TEST_TIMING_FACTOR` must widen the gap between the awaited
.claude/CLAUDE.md:290: trailing whitespace.
+action and the check that follows it.** A test obeys it when both sides of a comparison scale
.claude/CLAUDE.md:291: trailing whitespace.
+together, or when its slack is a deterministic constant such as the mocked read time. It breaks the
.claude/CLAUDE.md:292: trailing whitespace.
+rule when the slack is real, unscaled latency — thread wake-up, server start-up, converter work —
.claude/CLAUDE.md:293: trailing whitespace.
+because that stays the same size however high the factor goes. Such a test cannot be stabilised by
.claude/CLAUDE.md:294: trailing whitespace.
+raising the factor, which is the symptom to look for: if a failure rate is indifferent to the
.claude/CLAUDE.md:295: trailing whitespace.
+factor, the margin that decides it is not scaling. Running the suite at two factors is the direct
.claude/CLAUDE.md:296: trailing whitespace.
+check.
.claude/CLAUDE.md:297: trailing whitespace.
+
.claude/CLAUDE.md:298: trailing whitespace.
+This applies to the daemon as much as to the tests. #128 was a publish gate comparing wall clock
.claude/CLAUDE.md:299: trailing whitespace.
+against the poll cadence, with a sub-millisecond margin that no timing factor could widen, and it
.claude/CLAUDE.md:300: trailing whitespace.
+surfaced as a test that looked flaky but was reporting a real defect.
.claude/CLAUDE.md:301: trailing whitespace.
+
.claude/CLAUDE.md:302: trailing whitespace.
+- **Always express durations via `timing::milliseconds(n)` / `timing::seconds(n)`**, never a raw
.claude/CLAUDE.md:303: trailing whitespace.
+  `std::chrono::milliseconds(n)`. Each call multiplies `n` by the global `sFactor`
.claude/CLAUDE.md:304: trailing whitespace.
+  (`MQM_TEST_TIMING_FACTOR`; default `10` in `NDEBUG`/release, `1` in debug). A test that hardcodes a
.claude/CLAUDE.md:305: trailing whitespace.
+  raw literal for a wait or a configured `refresh` will pass at factor 1 and flake at factor 10.
.claude/CLAUDE.md:306: trailing whitespace.
+  `timing::defaultWait` (5s × factor) and `timing::maxTestTime` (10s × factor) are the standard
.claude/CLAUDE.md:307: trailing whitespace.
+  timeout constants. `TestConfig::toString()` rewrites the YAML's time values by the same factor, so
.claude/CLAUDE.md:308: trailing whitespace.
+  config durations and test-side waits scale together.
.claude/CLAUDE.md:309: trailing whitespace.
+- **Don't sleep-then-assert; wait on the event.** The mocks expose blocking helpers that wake on a
.claude/CLAUDE.md:310: trailing whitespace.
+  condition variable as soon as the awaited thing happens (or time out): `MockedMqttImpl` —
.claude/CLAUDE.md:311: trailing whitespace.
+  `waitForPublish`, `waitForMqttValue`, `waitForSubscription`, `waitForFirstPublish`,
.claude/CLAUDE.md:312: trailing whitespace.
+  `waitForRpcResponse`; `MockedModbusContext`/`MockedModbusFactory` — `waitForModbusValue`,
.claude/CLAUDE.md:313: trailing whitespace.
+  `waitForInitialPoll`. These are the synchronization primitive; polling with sleeps is both slower
.claude/CLAUDE.md:314: trailing whitespace.
+  and flakier.
.claude/CLAUDE.md:315: trailing whitespace.
+- **The mocked Modbus context simulates command duration.** Each slave has `mReadTime`/`mWriteTime`
.claude/CLAUDE.md:316: trailing whitespace.
+  (`sDefaultSlaveReadTime`/`WriteTime`, overridable per-slave via
.claude/CLAUDE.md:317: trailing whitespace.
+  `MockedModbusFactory::setModbusReadTime`/`setModbusWriteTime`) so reads/writes take wall-clock time
.claude/CLAUDE.md:318: trailing whitespace.

.claude/CLAUDE.md:319: trailing whitespace.

.claude/CLAUDE.md:320: trailing whitespace.

.claude/CLAUDE.md:321: trailing whitespace.

.claude/CLAUDE.md:322: trailing whitespace.

.claude/CLAUDE.md:323: trailing whitespace.

.claude/CLAUDE.md:324: trailing whitespace.

.claude/CLAUDE.md:328: trailing whitespace.

README.md:71: trailing whitespace.
+A multithreaded C++ service that enables two-way communication and data conversion between multiple [Modbus](http://www.modbus.org/) networks and [MQTT](http://mqtt.org/) clients.
README.md:72: trailing whitespace.
+
README.md:73: trailing whitespace.
+![docker build](https://github.com/BlackZork/mqmgateway/actions/workflows/main.yml/badge.svg)
README.md:74: trailing whitespace.
+
README.md:75: trailing whitespace.
+Main features:
README.md:76: trailing whitespace.
+
README.md:77: trailing whitespace.
+* Connects to multiple TCP and RTU modbus networks
README.md:78: trailing whitespace.
+* Handles state and availability for each configured MQTT object
README.md:79: trailing whitespace.
+* Allows reading and writing to MODBUS registers from MQTT side with custom data conversion
README.md:80: trailing whitespace.
+* Flexible MQTT state topic configuration:
README.md:81: trailing whitespace.
+  * single modbus register published as string value
README.md:82: trailing whitespace.
+  * multiple modbus registers as JSON object
README.md:83: trailing whitespace.
+  * multiple modbus registers as JSON list
README.md:84: trailing whitespace.
+  * registers from different slaves combined as single JSON list/object
README.md:85: trailing whitespace.
+  * publish on change or after every modbus poll, configurable per topic
README.md:86: trailing whitespace.
+* Full control over modbus data polling
README.md:87: trailing whitespace.
+  * read multiple register values once for multiple topics
README.md:88: trailing whitespace.
+  * read multiple register values for a single topic one by one
README.md:89: trailing whitespace.
+  * read multiple register values for a single topic once
README.md:90: trailing whitespace.
+  * registers used in multiple MQTT topics are polled only once
README.md:91: trailing whitespace.
+* Data conversion:
README.md:92: trailing whitespace.
+  * single register value to MQTT converters
README.md:93: trailing whitespace.
+  * multiple registers values to single MQTT value converters
README.md:94: trailing whitespace.
+  * support for [exprtk](https://github.com/ArashPartow/exprtk) expressions language when converting data
README.md:95: trailing whitespace.
+  * support for custom conversion plugins
README.md:96: trailing whitespace.
+  * support for conversion in both directions
README.md:97: trailing whitespace.
+* Fast modbus frequency polling, configurable per network, per MQTT object and per register
README.md:98: trailing whitespace.
+* Out of the box compatibility with [HomeAssistant](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/mqtt/) and [OpenHAB](https://www.openhab.org/addons/bindings/mqtt/) interfaces
README.md:99: trailing whitespace.

README.md:100: trailing whitespace.

+modqmttd has six log levels: *critical, error, warning, info, debug, trace*, numbered from 1 to 6. When debugging, you can increase the default *info* log level by passing `--loglevel <level>` to modmqttd:
README.md:171: trailing whitespace.

README.md:172: trailing whitespace.

README.md:173: trailing whitespace.
+modmqttd --config=<path> --loglevel=trace
README.md:174: trailing whitespace.

README.md:175: trailing whitespace.

+or setting log_level in `config.yaml`
README.md:177: trailing whitespace.
+
README.md:178: trailing whitespace.
+DEBUG is more useful for general troubleshooting, TRACE generates a lot of output and is not recommended for production use.

+* mqtt section contains MQTT broker connection parameters and modbus register mappings to MQTT topics
README.md:187: trailing whitespace.
+

README.md:758: trailing whitespace.
+
README.md:759: trailing whitespace.
+Data read from modbus registers is by default converted to string and published to MQTT broker.
README.md:760: trailing whitespace.
+
README.md:761: trailing whitespace.
+modmqttd uses conversion plugins to convert state data read from modbus registers to MQTT value and command MQTT payload to register value, for example to combine multiple modbus registers into single value, use mask to extract one bit, or perform some simple divide operations.
README.md:762: trailing whitespace.
+
README.md:763: trailing whitespace.

README.md:764: trailing whitespace.
+
README.md:765: trailing whitespace.

README.md:766: trailing whitespace.

README.md:767: trailing whitespace.
+```yaml
README.md:768: trailing whitespace.
+  converter: std.divide(20, low_first=true)
README.md:769: trailing whitespace.

README.md:770: trailing whitespace.

README.md:771: trailing whitespace.
+```
README.md:772: trailing whitespace.

README.md:773: trailing whitespace.

README.md:774: trailing whitespace.
+`std.int32`, four for `std.int64`. When the configured `count` does not match, modmqttd reports it
README.md:775: trailing whitespace.

README.md:777: trailing whitespace.

README.md:778: trailing whitespace.

README.md:779: trailing whitespace.

+## MQTT5 RPC interface
README.md:1357: trailing whitespace.
+
README.md:1358: trailing whitespace.
+The RPC interface lets an operator read or write **arbitrary** modbus registers on a
README.md:1359: trailing whitespace.
+running `modmqttd` without changing the configuration file. It is intended for commissioning
README.md:1360: trailing whitespace.
+and debugging — not for steady-state data flow, which is handled by the polled
README.md:1361: trailing whitespace.
+`state`/`commands` topics described above.
README.md:1362: trailing whitespace.
+
README.md:1363: trailing whitespace.
+A request is an MQTT5 request/response exchange: the client publishes a JSON request to
README.md:1364: trailing whitespace.
+`<client_id>/rpc/modbus_request` and `modmqttd` replies once to the MQTT5 *Response Topic*
README.md:1365: trailing whitespace.
+set on that request.
README.md:1366: trailing whitespace.
+
README.md:1367: trailing whitespace.
+### Enabling RPC
README.md:1368: trailing whitespace.
+
README.md:1369: trailing whitespace.
+RPC is disabled by default. Enable it in the `mqtt` section:
README.md:1370: trailing whitespace.
+
README.md:1371: trailing whitespace.
+```yaml
README.md:1372: trailing whitespace.
+mqtt:
README.md:1373: trailing whitespace.
+  client_id: myclient
README.md:1374: trailing whitespace.
+  rpc:
README.md:1375: trailing whitespace.
+    mode: readwrite
README.md:1376: trailing whitespace.
+  broker:
README.md:1377: trailing whitespace.
+    host: localhost
README.md:1378: trailing whitespace.
+```
README.md:1379: trailing whitespace.
+
README.md:1380: trailing whitespace.
+`mode` is one of:
README.md:1381: trailing whitespace.
+
README.md:1382: trailing whitespace.
+* `disabled` (default) — no RPC. The broker connection stays MQTT 3.1.1 and nothing changes.
README.md:1383: trailing whitespace.
+* `read` — register reads are allowed; writes are rejected.
README.md:1384: trailing whitespace.
+* `readwrite` — register reads and writes are allowed.
README.md:1385: trailing whitespace.
+
README.md:1386: trailing whitespace.
+Enabling RPC (`read` or `readwrite`) switches the **whole broker connection to MQTT 5**,
README.md:1387: trailing whitespace.
+because the request/response exchange relies on MQTT5 properties (Response Topic,
README.md:1388: trailing whitespace.
+Correlation Data, User Properties). The protocol version is per-connection and backward
README.md:1389: trailing whitespace.
+compatible, so ordinary MQTT 3.1.1 subscribers of your `state`/`command` topics are
README.md:1390: trailing whitespace.
+unaffected.
README.md:1391: trailing whitespace.
+
README.md:1392: trailing whitespace.
+The request topic is always `<client_id>/rpc/modbus_request`, where `<client_id>` is the
README.md:1393: trailing whitespace.
+`mqtt.client_id` value.
README.md:1394: trailing whitespace.
+
README.md:1395: trailing whitespace.
+### Request format
README.md:1396: trailing whitespace.
+
README.md:1397: trailing whitespace.
+The request payload is a JSON object with the following fields:
README.md:1398: trailing whitespace.
+
README.md:1399: trailing whitespace.
+* **network** (string, required)
README.md:1400: trailing whitespace.
+
README.md:1401: trailing whitespace.
+  Modbus network name, as defined in `modbus.networks[].name`.
README.md:1402: trailing whitespace.
+
README.md:1403: trailing whitespace.
+* **slave** (integer, required)
README.md:1404: trailing whitespace.
+
README.md:1405: trailing whitespace.
+  Modbus slave address.
README.md:1406: trailing whitespace.
+
README.md:1407: trailing whitespace.
+* **register** (string, required)
README.md:1408: trailing whitespace.
+
README.md:1409: trailing whitespace.
+  Register number. As elsewhere in the config, a decimal number is 1-based (first register
README.md:1410: trailing whitespace.
+  is `1`) and a hexadecimal number (`0x...`) is 0-based (first register is `0`).
README.md:1411: trailing whitespace.
+
README.md:1412: trailing whitespace.
+* **register_type** (string, optional)
README.md:1413: trailing whitespace.
+
README.md:1414: trailing whitespace.
+  One of `holding` (default), `input`, `coil` or `bit`.
README.md:1415: trailing whitespace.
+
README.md:1416: trailing whitespace.
+* **count** (integer, optional)
README.md:1417: trailing whitespace.
+
README.md:1418: trailing whitespace.
+  Number of registers to read, or — for a converter write — the number of registers the
README.md:1419: trailing whitespace.
+  value occupies. Default `1`. Range `1..125` for `holding`/`input`, `1..2000` for
README.md:1420: trailing whitespace.
+  `coil`/`bit`.
README.md:1421: trailing whitespace.
+
README.md:1422: trailing whitespace.
+* **value** (scalar or array, optional)
README.md:1423: trailing whitespace.
+
README.md:1424: trailing whitespace.
+  Presence makes the request a write; without it the request is a read.
README.md:1425: trailing whitespace.
+
README.md:1426: trailing whitespace.
+* **converter** (string, optional)
README.md:1427: trailing whitespace.
+
README.md:1428: trailing whitespace.
+  Converter to apply, e.g. `std.float32()`. Omitted, `""` or `"none"` means raw register

+### Response and errors
README.md:1475: trailing whitespace.
+
README.md:1476: trailing whitespace.
+`modmqttd` always replies once to the request's MQTT5 Response Topic, echoing the request's
README.md:1477: trailing whitespace.
+Correlation Data (if any). Replies are never retained. A request without a Response Topic
README.md:1478: trailing whitespace.
+cannot be answered and is logged and dropped.
README.md:1479: trailing whitespace.
+
README.md:1480: trailing whitespace.
+**Non-empty payload means success; empty payload means error.**
README.md:1481: trailing whitespace.
+
README.md:1482: trailing whitespace.
+On success the payload carries the register value(s):
README.md:1483: trailing whitespace.
+- **Read** — same scalar/array format as a polled state topic: a bare number string for a
README.md:1484: trailing whitespace.
+  single register (`"42"`), a JSON array for multiple (`"[10,20]"`). If a converter was
README.md:1485: trailing whitespace.
+  specified, the converter's string value is returned instead.
README.md:1486: trailing whitespace.
+- **Write** — the raw uint16 value(s) that were written, in the same scalar/array format
README.md:1487: trailing whitespace.
+  (`"77"` for one register, `"[10,20]"` for multiple). The converter is not re-applied on the
README.md:1488: trailing whitespace.
+  reply; what you get back are the actual register words that were sent to the device. 
README.md:1489: trailing whitespace.
+
README.md:1490: trailing whitespace.
+On error the payload is empty and an `error` MQTT5 User Property carries the message. Typical
README.md:1491: trailing whitespace.
+errors include an unknown network, a read-only register type for a write, a write attempted in
README.md:1492: trailing whitespace.
+`read` mode, an unknown or invalid converter, or a modbus read/write failure.

README.md:1495: trailing whitespace.
+
README.md:1496: trailing whitespace.
+**No response from `mosquitto_rr`**
README.md:1497: trailing whitespace.
+
README.md:1498: trailing whitespace.
+If `mosquitto_rr` hangs or times out, the request never reached `modmqttd` or `modmqttd`
README.md:1499: trailing whitespace.
+did not send a reply. Use `-W <seconds>` to set a client-side deadline:
README.md:1500: trailing whitespace.
+
README.md:1501: trailing whitespace.
+```bash
README.md:1502: trailing whitespace.
+mosquitto_rr -h <host> -t myclient/rpc/modbus_request -e myclient/rpc/reply -W 10 \
README.md:1503: trailing whitespace.
+  -m '{"network":"net1","slave":1,"register":"1"}'
README.md:1504: trailing whitespace.
+```
README.md:1505: trailing whitespace.
+
README.md:1506: trailing whitespace.
+Check that:
README.md:1507: trailing whitespace.

README.md:1508: trailing whitespace.
+- The topic prefix matches `mqtt.client_id` in the config exactly.
README.md:1509: trailing whitespace.
+- `modmqttd` is connected to the same broker as the test client.
README.md:1510: trailing whitespace.
+
README.md:1511: trailing whitespace.
+**Empty `(null)` response — reading the error message**
README.md:1512: trailing whitespace.
+
README.md:1513: trailing whitespace.
+`mosquitto_rr` does not display MQTT5 User Properties, so an error reply (empty payload +
README.md:1514: trailing whitespace.
+`error` property) looks like an empty response with no explanation. To see the `error`
README.md:1515: trailing whitespace.
+property, subscribe as an MQTT5 client with JSON output format in one terminal:
README.md:1516: trailing whitespace.
+
README.md:1517: trailing whitespace.
+```bash
README.md:1518: trailing whitespace.
+mosquitto_sub -h <host> -V mqttv5 -t myclient/rpc/reply -C 1 -W 10 -F '%j'
README.md:1519: trailing whitespace.
+```
README.md:1520: trailing whitespace.
+
README.md:1521: trailing whitespace.

README.md:1522: trailing whitespace.

+mosquitto_pub -h <host> -t myclient/rpc/modbus_request \
README.md:1525: trailing whitespace.

README.md:1526: trailing whitespace.
+  -m '{"network":"net1","slave":1,"register":"1"}'

README.md:1556: trailing whitespace.

README.md:1557: trailing whitespace.

README.md:1559: trailing whitespace.

README.md:1560: trailing whitespace.

readerwriterqueue/README.md:2: trailing whitespace.
+# A single-producer, single-consumer lock-free queue for C++
readerwriterqueue/README.md:3: trailing whitespace.
+
readerwriterqueue/README.md:4: trailing whitespace.
+This mini-repository has my very own implementation of a lock-free queue (that I designed from scratch) for C++.
readerwriterqueue/README.md:5: trailing whitespace.
+
readerwriterqueue/README.md:6: trailing whitespace.
+It only supports a two-thread use case (one consuming, and one producing). The threads can't switch roles, though
readerwriterqueue/README.md:7: trailing whitespace.
+you could use this queue completely from a single thread if you wish (but that would sort of defeat the purpose!).
readerwriterqueue/README.md:8: trailing whitespace.
+
readerwriterqueue/README.md:9: trailing whitespace.
+Note: If you need a general-purpose multi-producer, multi-consumer lock free queue, I have [one of those too][mpmc].
readerwriterqueue/README.md:10: trailing whitespace.
+
readerwriterqueue/README.md:11: trailing whitespace.
+This repository also includes a [circular-buffer SPSC queue][circular] which supports blocking on enqueue as well as dequeue.
readerwriterqueue/README.md:12: trailing whitespace.
+
readerwriterqueue/README.md:13: trailing whitespace.
+
readerwriterqueue/README.md:14: trailing whitespace.
+## Features
readerwriterqueue/README.md:15: trailing whitespace.
+
readerwriterqueue/README.md:16: trailing whitespace.
+- [Blazing fast][benchmarks]
readerwriterqueue/README.md:17: trailing whitespace.
+- Compatible with C++11 (supports moving objects instead of making copies)
readerwriterqueue/README.md:18: trailing whitespace.
+- Fully generic (templated container of any type) -- just like `std::queue`, you never need to allocate memory for elements yourself
readerwriterqueue/README.md:19: trailing whitespace.
+  (which saves you the hassle of writing a lock-free memory manager to hold the elements you're queueing)
readerwriterqueue/README.md:20: trailing whitespace.
+- Allocates memory up front, in contiguous blocks
readerwriterqueue/README.md:21: trailing whitespace.
+- Provides a `try_enqueue` method which is guaranteed never to allocate memory (the queue starts with an initial capacity)
readerwriterqueue/README.md:22: trailing whitespace.
+- Also provides an `enqueue` method which can dynamically grow the size of the queue as needed
readerwriterqueue/README.md:23: trailing whitespace.
+- Also provides `try_emplace`/`emplace` convenience methods
readerwriterqueue/README.md:24: trailing whitespace.
+- Has a blocking version with `wait_dequeue`
readerwriterqueue/README.md:25: trailing whitespace.
+- Completely "wait-free" (no compare-and-swap loop). Enqueue and dequeue are always O(1) (not counting memory allocation)
readerwriterqueue/README.md:26: trailing whitespace.
+- On x86, the memory barriers compile down to no-ops, meaning enqueue and dequeue are just a simple series of loads and stores (and branches)
readerwriterqueue/README.md:27: trailing whitespace.
+
readerwriterqueue/README.md:28: trailing whitespace.
+
readerwriterqueue/README.md:29: trailing whitespace.
